claims.text: The initial CrMnFeCoNi-type alloy is homogenized and single-phase, with uniform elemental distribution and minimal pre-existing precipitates.
The initial homogenized HEA has high toughness and ductility under ambient conditions.
The initial alloy has no significant grain-boundary precipitates under ambient conditions.
Exposure near 700°C under mechanical loading can cause Cr, Ni, and Mn to segregate to grain boundaries in CrMnFeCoNi HEAs.
Mechanical deformation facilitates diffusion and segregation of susceptible elements to grain boundaries.
Cyclic loading specifically promotes the proposed grain-boundary segregation process.
Mn is a segregation-prone minor element in the proposed CrMnFeCoNi-type alloy.
Segregation of Cr, Ni, and Mn in CrMnFeCoNi can produce grain-boundary nanoclustering and phase separation.
Cr-rich BCC phases and L10-NiMn phases can precipitate at grain boundaries in Cr20Mn20Fe20Co20Ni20.
Cr-rich sigma phases can form after deformation-assisted grain-boundary diffusion and annealing in CrMnFeCoNi HEAs.
Prolonged aging near 700°C combined with cyclic loading will nucleate brittle intergranular precipitates.
Grain-boundary segregation and nanoclustering can reduce grain-boundary cohesion and cause intergranular decohesion.
Brittle grain-boundary intermetallic phases substantially reduce ductility in CrMnFeCoNi HEAs.
The segregation-prone alloy will show a marked reduction in ductility and toughness relative to a modified alloy with reduced segregation.
The modified alloy will better retain toughness under otherwise identical aging and cyclic-loading conditions.
TEM or APT will reveal brittle intergranular precipitates in the segregation-prone alloy after the proposed treatment.
The proposed embrittlement mechanism should be most prominent during prolonged high-temperature exposure combined with cyclic loading.
The proposed embrittlement effects should be minimal at low temperature or under static loading.
Comparing a standard alloy with a variant in which Mn is reduced, replaced, or inhibited provides a control for testing the segregation mechanism.
Absence of both intergranular precipitates and mechanical degradation in both tested alloys would falsify the proposed mechanism under the tested conditions.

contradictions.description: Mn is characterized as a minor element, but the exemplar CrMnFeCoNi system conventionally treats Mn as one of the principal constituent elements; no minor Mn concentration is specified.
